title: Region provisioning intake adjudication and SLA template for enterprise residency requests
creator: Priya Anand
description:
Objective: Create a repeatable intake form, numeric adjudication matrix, and a negotiable SLA template that product + sales + customer engineering can use to evaluate enterprise geography/residency requests (new region provisioning, data residency guarantees, and failover topology asks).

Scope: non-bug enterprise requests only. Covers: new public region enablement (cloud region onboarding), VPC/private deployment residency constraints, and documented failover/DR topologies for cross-region continuity. Excludes: low-touch self-serve region preferences for hosted customers (handled by existing region flags).

Deliverables: 
- Intake form fields and example responses (legal/regulatory citation, data category, in-region data egress restrictions, expected QPS, peak concurrency, revenue at stake, contract term).
- Adjudication matrix with weighted scoring for: regulatory constraint (weight 30), customer revenue and strategic value (20), capacity/cost delta (20), latency delta & UX impact (15), operational complexity (10), rollback/failover feasibility (5).
- Minimum thresholds and decision outcomes: auto-approve, sales-assisted review, product-led roadmap entry, or decline.
- SLA template draft with RTO/RPO options, latency SLO bands, capacity commit tiers, and failover routing commitments.
- Playbook for failover design patterns and safe defaults (active-active, active-passive, regional mirror with warm standby).

Decision criteria summary: 
- Regulatory must-haves (hard blocker): data residency law citation, required in-country storage, mandatory audit/KMS controls.
- Capacity economics: estimated incremental monthly cost at 50th and 95th percentile load; required Dedicated/reserved vs hosted burst.
- Technical feasibility: model compatibility (quantization/ops), runtime kernel support in target region, ability to meet latency SLOs.
- Customer SLA need: contract-backed SLAs require Dedicated/Private and runbook integration.

Trade-offs discussed: 
- Tight residency guarantees increase unit costs and operational overhead; recommend packaging as premium add-on with minimum commit.
- For failover, active-active reduces RTO but doubles steady-state cost; warm-standby can be a compromise for P1 customers.
- Rapid region enablement may require temporary soft guarantees (migration window) while audits and KMS integrations complete.

SLA template highlights (summary): 
- Availability commitments: 99.9% for hosted-residency tier, 99.95% for Dedicated-residency tier (per contract).
- Latency SLOs: p95 generation latency <= configured band (example: <=200ms for short prompts, <=500ms for long sequences), with tokenized billing adjustments for QoS processing.
- Failover commitments: documented failover path and RTO (1 hour for warm-standby, 15 minutes for active-active with dns/anycast automation).
- Data handling: KMS/HSM integration clause, in-region key custody options, audit log retention windows.

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field below.

Notes: This ticket ties directly to Dedicated capacity sizing and Runtime kernel availability work owned by ENG. We need a gating checklist that prevents premature promises to customers.

Next steps: 
1) Validate matrix weights with Sales Ops and Legal (owner: Marcus Liu).
2) Run three representative adjudication exercises using recent inbound requests (owners: PM + Solutions Eng).
3) Draft SLA PDF and an editable Google Docs template for contract negotiations.
4) Produce a short runbook for CS/SE to follow post-signing.

Estimate rationale: 8 points to cover stakeholder interviews, three intake simulations, SLA drafting, and initial legal review.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form fields and example responses published to Confluence
Adjudication matrix with numeric weights and decision thresholds documented
Three simulated requests adjudicated and outcomes logged against matrix
SLA template draft reviewed by Legal and Sales Ops
Failover playbook and recommended defaults published to Console docs
Handoff checklist to ENG and Customer Engineering created
